PP2 · Chapter 6 of 7

Follow the picture clues

Use positions, arrows and two visible clues.

  1. See it
  2. Try it
  3. Practise it
  4. Print it
  5. Check it

This chapter works best after Find the pattern. You can still look around, or jump to the check.

By the end I can…

  • I can find a place in a row.
  • I can choose a picture using two clues.
  • I can follow arrows on a map.

1 See it

Screen 1 of 3

Places in a row

The ball is 1st. The apple is 2nd.

The star is 3rd. The heart is 4th.

The fish is 5th and last.

Screen 2 of 3

Use two clues

Clue 1: it is red.

Clue 2: it is round.

Only the apple is red and round.

Screen 3 of 3

Follow the arrows

Arrows tell the robot where to go.

North is up. East is right.

Go up, up, then right, right to reach the goal.

Words to know
clue
A small hint that helps you find the answer.
first, last
First is at the start. Last is at the end.
arrow
It points which way to go.

2 Try it

Now you do it. Move the pieces, then press Check my answer.

Activity 1

Put the picture that is red and round in the first box.

Turn on JavaScript to move the pieces.

Activity 2

Make the robot reach the goal. Add arrows, then press Run.

Turn on JavaScript to move the pieces.

Activity 3

The row is ball, apple, star, heart, fish. Tap the place of the fish.

Turn on JavaScript to move the pieces.

Chapter passed. Next: Days, months and clocks

For parents

What your child learns

Your child finds a place in a row, picks a picture using two clues, and follows arrows. These are the first steps of logic and coding.

A common slip

Using only one clue. Say each clue aloud and cross out pictures that do not match.

5-minute home activity: Treasure hunt

  1. Hide a toy in the room.
  2. Give two clues: "It is soft. It is on the sofa."
  3. Then give arrow steps: two steps forward, one step left.
  4. Swap and let your child give the clues.
